Definition: probably to brighten up, i.e. (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome
BiblicalUsage: The word sâmach means to brighten up, that is (figuratively) be (causatively, make) blithe or gleesome. In 1 Chronicles 16:10, we read, "…holy name: let the heart of them rejoice…"; in 1 Kings 5:7, "…Blessed the LORD this day, which hath given…". You hear it again in 1 Samuel 2:1 — "…My heart rejoiceth in the LORD, mine horn…" — and in 2 Chronicles 6:41, "Now therefore arise, O LORD God, into thy…".
TheologicalSignificance: I believe sâmach is the Lord's own word, and it shows his people what he is like. I hold that sâmach still speaks, because the God who spoke then has not changed.
